```{r}
library(broom)
library(here)
library(PNWColors)
```

## 1. Is medical history related to cardiac events?

### 1.1 Introduction

Stress echocardiography is used to detect coronary artery disease and to estimate which patients are at risk of future cardiac problems. In the UCLA dataset used here (Garfinkel et al., 1999), 558 patients had a dobutamine stress echocardiogram and were followed for one year. During follow-up Garfinkel et al. recorded whether each patient had a new heart attack, an angioplasty, bypass surgery or died of cardiac causes. We combine these into a single outcome, `any event`.

Before the test, each patient's medical history was recorded: **hypertension**, **diabetes**, **smoking**, **prior heart attack**, **prior angioplasty** and **prior bypass surgery**. Established heart disease and cardiovascular risk factors are plausibly linked to more future events.

So, firstly, it is sensible to ask oneself, is a patient's prior history associated with having a cardiac event within one year of the stress test?

### 1.2 Data preparation

Despite the data has been already cleaned up, it is sensible to simplify the data set to the variables which are planned to be used.

```{r}
MedicalHData <- stressEcho |> 
  select(AnyEvent, RecentMyocardialInfarction, RecentAngioplasty,
         RecentBypassSurgery, death, HypertensionHistory,
         DiabetesHistory, SmokingHistory, MyocardialInfarctionHistory,
         AngioplastyHistory, BypassSurgeryHistory, age, gender)
```

`BurdenScore` variable is created. It will consist on a score given to each patient depending on the their clinical history (Scores go from 0 to 6). Smoking history is divided in three categories: `non-smokers`, `moderate` and `heavy`. For the purpose of our analysis, we are simplifying to `non-smokers` and `smokers`.

```{r}
MedicalHData <- MedicalHData |>
  mutate(
      HypertensionHistory = case_when(HypertensionHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                      HypertensionHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      DiabetesHistory = case_when(DiabetesHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                  DiabetesHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      MyocardialInfarctionHistory = case_when(MyocardialInfarctionHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                              MyocardialInfarctionHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      AngioplastyHistory = case_when(AngioplastyHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                     AngioplastyHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      BypassSurgeryHistory = case_when(BypassSurgeryHistory == "yes" ~ 1,
                                       BypassSurgeryHistory == "no" ~ 0),
      SmokingHistory = case_when(SmokingHistory == "non-smoker" ~ 0,
                                 SmokingHistory == "heavy" ~ 1,
                                 SmokingHistory == "moderate" ~ 1),
      AnyEvent = case_when(AnyEvent == "yes" ~ 1,
                                       AnyEvent == "no" ~ 0),
    BurdenScore = HypertensionHistory + DiabetesHistory + 
      AngioplastyHistory + BypassSurgeryHistory + MyocardialInfarctionHistory + SmokingHistory
  )
```

### 1.3 Analysis

#### 1.3.1 Does the presence of the different histories affect the number of events in patients?

Only essential columns are chosen, data is pivoted longer for facilitating the summary of the whole data set. Three new variables are added to the data set: `n`, being the total number of occurrences for each history condition, `Events`, being the sum of patients having a cardiac event of any type during follow-up and `EventRate`, being the percentage of patients who have suffered cardiac events per clininal history.

```{r}
MedicalHLong <- MedicalHData |>
  select(
    c(HypertensionHistory, DiabetesHistory, AngioplastyHistory, BypassSurgeryHistory,
      MyocardialInfarctionHistory, SmokingHistory, AnyEvent)
  ) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(HypertensionHistory, DiabetesHistory, AngioplastyHistory,
             BypassSurgeryHistory, MyocardialInfarctionHistory, SmokingHistory),
    names_to = "History",
    values_to = "HistoryStatus"
  ) |> 
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    events = sum(AnyEvent),
    .by = c(History, HistoryStatus)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    EventRate = (events/n)*100,
    HistoryStatus = case_when(
      HistoryStatus == 1 ~ "with",
      HistoryStatus == 0 ~ "without"
      
    )
  )

MedicalHLong
```

```{r}
MeanAnyEvent <- MedicalHData |> 
  summarise(
    mean(AnyEvent) * 100
  )

EventRatesPerClinicalHPlot <- ggplot(data=MedicalHLong,
                                     aes(x = History,
                                         y = EventRate,
                                         fill = HistoryStatus)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = pull(MeanAnyEvent),
             linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25,
                                   hjust = 1),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  labs(x = "Medical history",
       y = "Event rate (%)", 
       title = "Event rates in patients with previous medical history",
       subtitle = "dashed line = overall rate (15.95%)",
       fill = "HistoryStatus"
       ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pnw_palette(name = "Starfish",
                                         n = 2))+
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("AngioplastyHistory" = "Angioplasty",
                              "BypassSurgeryHistory" = "Bypass surgery",
                              "DiabetesHistory" = "Diabetes",
                              "HypertensionHistory" = "Hypertension", 
                              "MyocardialInfarctionHistory" = "Myocardical infraction",
                              "SmokingHistory" = "Smoking"))


ggsave(filename = here("results/01_EventRatesPerClinicalHPlot.png"),
       plot = EventRatesPerClinicalHPlot)

EventRatesPerClinicalHPlot
```

#### 1.3.2 Does more history burden increase the probability of an event occurring?

A new subset is created. This time, `BurdenScore` variable is added to the selected subset to know if the accumulation of history factor along the follow-up increases the event rate. If four or more history factors, we accumulate them in an united category `4+` since few patients have many factors.

```{r}
BurdenScoreData <- MedicalHData |>
  select(
    c(BurdenScore, HypertensionHistory, DiabetesHistory, AngioplastyHistory,
      BypassSurgeryHistory, MyocardialInfarctionHistory, SmokingHistory, AnyEvent)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    BurdenScore = ifelse(BurdenScore >= 4,
                           "4+",
                           as.character(BurdenScore))
  ) |> 
  summarise(
    n=n(),
    events = sum(AnyEvent),
    .by = BurdenScore
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    EventRate = (events/n)*100,
  )

BurdenScoreData
```

```{r}
BurdenScorePlot <- ggplot(data=BurdenScoreData, aes(x = BurdenScore, y = EventRate)) +
  geom_col(fill=pnw_palette(name = "Starfish", n=1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = as.numeric(MeanAnyEvent), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  labs(x="History burden",
       y="Event rate (%)",
       title = "Event rates in patients with accumulative history",
       subtitle = "dashed line = overall rate (15.95%)")

ggsave(filename = here("results/01_BurdenScorePlot.png"),
       plot = BurdenScorePlot)

BurdenScorePlot
```

#### 1.3.3 Which variable has more effect on the occurrence of any cardiac event?

A logistic regression model is trained with our data to find out which out of all the variables chosen have a bigger effect on the occurrence of a cardiac event. These findings are presented in a forest plot as well as a data table.

```{r}
model <- MedicalHData |> 
  glm(formula = AnyEvent ~ age + gender + HypertensionHistory + DiabetesHistory + AngioplastyHistory + BypassSurgeryHistory + MyocardialInfarctionHistory + SmokingHistory,
      family = binomial)

ForestPlotData <- model |>
  tidy(conf.int = TRUE,
       exponentiate = TRUE) |> 
  filter(term != "(Intercept)")

ForestPlot <- ggplot(ForestPlotData, 
                     mapping = aes(x = estimate,
                                   y = fct_reorder(term, estimate))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, 
             linetype = "dashed") + 
  geom_errorbar(mapping = aes(xmin = conf.low,
                              xmax = conf.high),
                width = 0.2) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = c("AngioplastyHistory" = "Angioplasty",
                              "BypassSurgeryHistory" = "Bypass surgery",
                              "DiabetesHistory" = "Diabetes",
                              "HypertensionHistory" = "Hypertension", 
                              "MyocardialInfarctionHistory" = "Myocardial infarction",
                              "SmokingHistory" = "Smoking",
                              "gendermale" = "Male (vs female)",
                              "age" = "Age"))+
  labs(x = "Odds ratio (95% CI, log scale)",
       y=NULL, 
       title = "Adjusted odds ratios for a cardiac event within one year")

ggsave(filename = here("results/01_ForestPlot.png"),
       plot = ForestPlot)

ForestPlot
ForestPlotData
```
